pr_body:
Closes #67095.

As far as I understand, this property should not be stored in the scene file, but should be calculated depending on other properties and the type of the parent node.

`PROPERTY_USAGE_INTERNAL` is responsible for hiding the property in documentation, etc., but does not control the storage of the property, this is the responsibility of `PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE`, which is included in `PROPERTY_USAGE_DEFAULT`.

I tested and didn't find any regressions. "Layout Mode" is correctly restored after reloading the editor if a non-default "Anchors Preset" is selected.

However, I'd like to get confirmation from the feature implementer that `layout_mode` really shouldn't be saved in the scene file, since I haven't studied this code thoroughly.
pr_comments:
No, it should be stored for children of non-Containers. Users can pick between "Position" and "Anchors". If we don't save it, then it can resolve to "Position" even though user would have left it at "Anchors".

> `PROPERTY_USAGE_INTERNAL` is responsible for hiding the property in documentation, etc., but does not control the storage of the property,

Yep, that's why it is used there, as there is no other way to avoid documenting it AFAIK.

> If we don't save it, then it can resolve to "Position" even though user would have left it at "Anchors".

Maybe I missed something, but isn't "Anchors" with "Top Left" equal to "Position"?

> Maybe I missed something, but isn't "Anchors" with "Top Left" equal to "Position"?

That's why it would resolve as "Position" if we stop saving the property, yes. But that's not what a user might expect. If you pick the "Anchors" mode, you should be able to continue using it upon the restart/scene reload. Just because "Position" maps to one of the presets doesn't mean it's good usability to remove the ability to explicitly stay with "Anchors" and "Top Left".
Is that information useful for editor only? Maybe it should be stored in editor layout (that thing saved per-scene, grid settings, folding etc)?

I don't think this one counts as a user preference to be stored in the editor project cache. Yes, it's useful only in the editor, but it's a part of each control's setup, that makes sense to share between collaborators in a team. I think the choice to use "Anchors" with "Top Left" instead of "Position" is a conscious one most of the time.

@YuriSizov It seems to me that it doesn't matter, because if the user has selected "Anchors", then only to change the preset (or set custom anchors), but not to use the default "Top Left", which corresponds to "Position". It doesn't make sense. If the user stopped in the middle of the path, then they actually does not change anything, and when restarting the editor, rolling back to the beginning makes sense. There is no need to commit intermediate state.

So `layout_mode` is a completely "virtual property", just to hide irrelevant properties and to help users who don't understand the difference between manual positioning, anchors, and containers. We could not use "Layout Mode" at all, but just hide/lock "Anchor Presets" in cases where it shouldn't change.

It's an implementation detail that position and top left preset are the same. To the user, they've made a choice to use the Anchors mode and in that mode they might pick the "Top Left" preset. If you set you scene up like that, then open it again and see a different result, that's not good. Furthermore, the fact that we _consistently_ save the property when our user changes it is not a bug, and not something that should be fixed. If we have an inconsistency, then that's a bug and that should be fixed instead.

I.e. the property should not randomly appear and disappear in the scene file. It should only do so when it makes sense, e.g. when the user changed it to a non-default value for a node where saving state matters.
Two different states denoting the same thing is not good. Users will think there is a difference between them when there is no difference.

There is a difference in respect to what the goal is: to use the anchor presets or not to use them. The position mode is not a replacement for presets, it's just a simplified version of the anchors mode. If the user opts out of using the simplified version, we must respect that. And it costs us absolutely nothing to do so.

Switching "Layout Mode" to "Anchors" while leaving the default "Top Left" preset does not provide any benefit to the user. I don't think this setup makes any sense to share with collaborators (and even save between editor restarts / scene reopens). This is a phantom, artificial difference with no practical use.

The discussion is getting a little bit of a sophistry, so I'll stop here and wait for the opinion of the maintainers.

---

In my opinion, the "Layout Mode" property is not needed at all. We could just hide/block the "Anchors Preset" if it's a child of a container or has no parent. "Layout Mode" duplicates this hint, and is not a real mode that affects the behavior of the Control:

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47700418/206892124-aa078574-3f07-4136-929d-11674790ed7c.png)

And besides, it adds 2 extra clicks to switch "mode". Basically, the only purpose of the "Layout Mode" property is to hide/show another property ("Anchors Preset").

The purpose of "Layout Mode" is to provide 2 different ways to configure controls. One is simple where you only edit position and size, and another is more advanced where you can edit anchors too. This was an important part of the original proposal and is implemented this way for this specific purpose. For Container-controlled and for uncontrolled nodes this field could be hidden, but keeping it visible and with a sensible, corresponding value serves as a clue to the user. It shows that controls can exist in different modes and that some of those modes are contextual, and some you can pick on your own.

> We could just hide/block the "Anchors Preset" if it's a child of a container or has no parent.

We already do. Position and Anchor modes are only available for children of other regular controls, they are not available for children of containers.

> "Layout Mode" duplicates this hint, and is not a real mode that affects the behavior of the Control

The hint is an extra, which elaborates on the state of the control. The property itself is a part of the state itself. They overlap, but as noted at least in one state the user can pick the mode that they want to work in.

> The discussion is getting a little bit of a sophistry, so I'll stop here and wait for the opinion of the maintainers.

As the maintainer of this feature I'm trying to explain why certain design decisions were made. You are free to disagree, of course, and we can try other solutions. But there is a reason for the current behavior, and it is a meaningful property to have and to save. In terms of sharing it with other collaborators it's no different than `editor_only` on the light nodes.

We are trying to introduce 3 different ways to position controls, as per the original proposal that I implemented. One is for the simplest things, where you don't even want to think about anchors. One is for when you do need anchors. And one for when you are inside of a container. Whichever mode is available and is picked by the user should be preserved, because whether or not you think it's ultimately sensible or logical, it's user's choice to pick "Anchors". I don't understand how it would improve things if we decided to switch it back to "Position" without user's consent just to save one line in the scene file. We aren't helping them, we're just trying to make things neat for ourselves.

And I repeat, that if there is a bug where the property appears and disappears in the scene files without user interaction, then that is indeed a problem that is worth fixing.

Here's how I see it. The top row is the current implementation, the bottom row is without "Layout Mode".

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47700418/206914273-ede0a8fc-768e-4c26-9cd9-2a6211798836.png)

For children of containers, we can hide the "Anchors Preset" instead of blocking.

If you want to remove the position mode completely, that's a separate issue. But it was added on purpose, as it was suggested in the proposal. Either way, it's out of scope of fixing the linked issue.

> For children of containers, we can hide the "Anchors Preset" instead of blocking.

Yes, you shouldn't make it visible. There are no anchors in containers.
Closing as based on the above discussion, and further comments in the issue, this doesn't seem to be the correct fix.

issue_context.title: Layout mode disappears randomly
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0 880a017

### System information

Windows 10 x64

### Issue description

I keep getting this kind of diffs all the time:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/194727086-6dcd94e3-775e-485c-9d9e-9aa631dcb6b0.png)
Happens randomly (might be related to project load with last opened scenes?) and re-saving the scene changes it back.

### Steps to reproduce

idk, it just happens

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments:
Reading the code, it doesn't seem to be meant to be saved at all, that's weird.
I saw several users mention that issue on Twitter (but also without steps to reproduce).

> Reading the code, it doesn't seem to be meant to be saved at all, that's weird. I saw several users mention that issue on Twitter (but also without steps to reproduce).

I provided steps to reproduce it in my issue, but I didn't know this one exists. I paste it here.

### Steps to reproduce

(the sample project can be found in my issue)

1) Open the sample project and open the 2 scenes included inside `test_layout_mode` and `another_scene`.
2) Check that the property `layout_mode` exists in `test_layout_mode` for almost all nodes.
3) Go to the scene `another_scene` and run the current scene (see the image).
4) Go to the file `test_layout_mode.tscn` and you will notice that the property `layout_mode` disappear from nodes.

**Note:** If you have another scenes opened, the property will disappear as well. It seems like all scenes opened in the editor will be impacted, but not the ones closed.

![CleanShot 2022-10-09 at 14 17 07@2x](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1923206/194756424-8a604754-5fbf-422c-99cf-b7536a471f84.png)

Here's a video to illustrate it:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1923206/194756160-4c159262-77aa-4c4b-9394-cf9483652858.mp4

I can confirm, the property `layout_mode` is removed from opened scenes (the ones in tab in the editor).

Plus, the property is added back to the scene you play.

The above comments by @Cronos87 has reminded me that my comment above is only one part of the solution for this issue.

In addition to Control always serializing properties that contain unused values, the state of Control's layout logic depends on it being in the SceneTree which is not available for scenes opened in background tabs in the editor as only the active tab is actually attached to the SceneTree. These two things combined results in Control serializing different properties depending on whether or not it is the active tab in the editor when the scene is saved. I have not solved this second issue myself and my above patch may actually make things worse depending on the scene's contents even if it's a step in the right direction.

The above reproduction steps assume that the `run/auto_save/save_before_running` editor setting is enabled before attempting to run the scene. An alternative step is to use the "Scene -> Save All Scenes" main menu option.

This has been vexing me for weeks and it's really helpful to have the explanation of what is happening and how to avoid it.  Thanks!

I don't know if this is helpful but I find that random changes of ``layout_mode`` are often accompanied by slight changes to ``offset_top`` and ``offset_bottom`` which also revert themselves when re-saved.

I'm getting this as well, which is confusing and makes me worry something will break. In most cases it doesn't seem to change anything in the game, but I suspect it could have caused an issue where an instanced GUI scene got mangled and I had to remove it and re-instance it to fix it.

In my case there seems to be some cycle where `layout_mode` is either added, removed or changed between 1 and 3 by some process I don't know the origin of. Rarely there will also be changes to offset_* properties. This seems to affect either 2D scenes (different menus) that are open in the editor when the game is run or instanced in 3d scenes that are open (like my game overlay scene instanced in my main game scene) even though I have made no changes to the files in question, only changing scripts and running again.

In the case of the instanced scenes (I suspect this is the problem in my case) I also think it might be related to the scenes being instanced with "editable children". I have this enabled to be able to connect some signals to/from children in the UI scenes, but it seems to also add overrides to layouts even though I haven't changed any of those properties. Perhaps the editor is sometimes incorrectly adding or modifying these overrides?

Edit: this is in 4.0.beta6
I am using beta 7 with Git and this problem is starting to get on my nerves.
Doesn't even look like it's on the radar for 4.0-final..!

> Doesn't even look like it's on the radar for 4.0-final..!

Contributors work on a best-effort basis, so there is no ETA for fixing issues in general.
I'm less concerned about when than before what version, happy to see it on the 4.0 milestone
I opened PR #69860. Please test if it fixes the issue and doesn't cause any regressions.

The PR does not solve this issue at all. This issue is not just that a single property changes when saved but rather the entire state of Control is invalid when it is attempted to be saved when it is not in the scene tree. See my two comments above.

Thinking this issue through I think that the easiest way to solve this is to have Control cache what its parent situation is when it is added to the tree as a hidden property, and update it when its parent changes. This property is stored so that it can be remembered across reloads even if it is never attached to the scene tree (e.g. loaded directly into a background tab). There are three situations: Parented to a Container, parented to another Control, or either parented to any other node or not parented at all.

Doing this, as well as ensuring that only authoritative properties are actually stored (see my first comment above), should solve the issue completely (which affects more than just the `layout_mode` property) without requiring more in-depth changes to Godot core.

I'm not aware of any other Node that changes which properties it uses based on what other Node it is attached too.

If it's any help, I did some tests to help narrow down the issue a little bit.  You can find them in this repo:
https://github.com/ashelleyPurdue/GodotResaveTest
@ashelleyPurdue Thanks for a thorough investigation, it's very helpful! The grow directions appearing is indeed a minor issue with the editor, for the rest I'll need to look into it more.

review_comments: Yes, it can be simplified to `PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR | PROPERTY_USAGE_INTERNAL` if we don't expect `PROPERTY_USAGE_DEFAULT` to change.
